title: Concierge SDK prototype flow - notebook
content:
Purpose:
This is a working notebook for a lightweight 'concierge' SDK onramp flow aimed at internal product teams that are spinning up prototype integrations with Redwood Inference. The goal: give engineers a 20–40 minute path from concept -> running prototype with telemetry and guardrails enabled, without forcing full SDK adoption immediately.

Context / why this exists:
- Lots of internal prototypes hit the same startup friction: keys, environment, simple HTTP vs SDK choice, missing telemetry, and unclear fallback behaviour.
- The concierge flow is a minimal bundle (single-page quickstart + tiny helper library + a preseeded sandbox route) that reduces cognitive overhead while preserving production patterns (retries, streaming, cost labels).
- This doc is intentionally informal: notes, checklist, sample curl + pseudo-SDK usage, telemetry hooks, and rollout plan.

Audience:
- PMs and Engs rapidly proving a feature with LLMs (search summarization, chat assistant, embedding-based recall).
- Solutions Engineers who onboard internal teams.
- Developer advocates building demo apps.

Assumptions:
- Team has Redwood account and sandbox API key with limited quotas.
- Quick sandbox route is pre-configured to point at a small hosted model variant (low-cost).
- Console has a one-click enable for 'concierge telemetry' that provisions a temp dataset and tracing hooks.

Quickstart (20–40 min):
1) 2-min: Create sandbox key
   - Sign into Console -> Team -> API keys -> create key -> label 'concierge-proto-YYYYMMDD'
2) 3-min: Clone the quickstart repo template (private internal repo)
   - git clone git@github.com:redwood/concierge-quickstarts.git && cd node-chat-stub
3) 5-min: env setup
   - copy .env.example -> .env, paste sandbox key, set SANDBOX_MODE=true
   - yarn install || npm install
4) 5–8 min: Run a smoke curl to verify endpoint
   - curl -X POST https://sandbox.redwood.ai/v1/concierge-chat \
     -H 'Authorization: Bearer <KEY>' \
     -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
     -d '{"prompt": "Write a 2-line intro for the demo app"}'
   - Expect 200 + streaming-friendly chunked body or small JSON response
5) 5–10 min: Switch to minimal helper (concierge-sdk-lite)
   - Node example: require('@redwood/concierge-lite').chat({key: process.env.KEY, trace:true})
   - call .send({messages:[...] }).on('data', chunk=>console.log(chunk))
6) 2–5 min: Flip on telemetry and run a sample session
   - Console -> Enable 'concierge telemetry' for the key -> use built-in sample prompt set
   - Confirm an event appears in the Temp Telemetry view (latency, tokens, model-id, route)

Minimal API contract (concierge-lite):
- chat(opts) -> returns a Session object with: send(message), on('data'), on('end'), on('error')
- embed(texts) -> returns Promise<array of vectors> (batched automatically)
- labelCost({route, costEstimate, tags}) -> soft annotation to demo cost-sensitive routing

Design constraints and opinions (short):
- Keep surface area tiny: only 3 functions we need. Avoid full SDK parity in this flow.
- Enable sensible defaults: 3 retries on 5xx, 250ms jitter, stream buffered every 200ms.
- Safety: block obviously disallowed outputs (use policy shim) before returning to prototype UI.
- Observability: every call emits a minimal trace id that maps to Console temp telemetry.

Telemetry & metrics to surface in quickstart UI:
- Request latency (p50/p95)
- Tokens consumed per session (input vs output)
- Model variant used and a flag if fallback occurred
- Error counts by class (auth, rate_limit, infra, model_error)
- Approx cost estimate (cheap heuristic: cost = tokens_out*model_rate_per_1k)

Sample minimal tracing payload (what concierge-lite emits):
- trace_id: generated UUID
- route: 'concierge-chat'
- model_hint: 'small-chat-v1'
- latency_ms: 84
- tokens_in: 24
- tokens_out: 78
- cost_estimate_cents: 2
- user_agent: 'concierge-quickstart/1.0'

Failure modes and recovery guidance (for champions):
- 401/403: usually key mis-scope; re-provision a sandbox key and ensure telemetry flag set
- 429: quota exhausted; Console -> request temporary bump or switch to offline stub
- 5xx or model OOM: automatic fallback to 'tiny-safe' variant after 2 retries; expose 'fallback' banner in demo UI
- Streaming stalls: concierge-lite includes a keepalive/heartbeat when streaming stalls > 3s

Acceptance checklist for an internal prototype handoff:
- [ ] Demo runs end-to-end with sample prompts
- [ ] Telemetry events appear in Console temp view for the key
- [ ] Error handling paths demonstrated (auth, quota, fallback)
- [ ] Cost estimate visible and explains the delta if switching models
- [ ] Security review quick sign-off (no PII in sample dataset)

Mini rollout plan (3 phases):
- Phase 0 (concierge): internal-only templates + short-lived keys, target 6 teams in month 1
- Phase 1 (adoptable): convert popular templates into first-class quickstarts in public/internal repo, add telemetry retention 7d
- Phase 2 (productize): fold into self-serve Console with opt-in telemetry and billing labels, add canned safety prompts

Instrumented experiments to run (30/60/90 days):
- Track conversion: how many concierge prototype keys turn into committed Dedicated usage within 90 days
- Latency sensitivity: which demo patterns trigger largest p95 regressions (long context vs many short calls)
- Feature toggles: measure adoption of embed+recall vs single-call summarization (which reduces tokens/cost?)

Open questions / TODOs (quick):
- Which preseed prompt sets should be included by default? (Ideas: email reply, meeting notes, product Q&A)
- Do we need an ephemeral UI for token/cost visualization, or reuse Console widgets?
- How to handle prototype data retention and deletion by default (7 days vs 30 days)?
- Can the helper library auto-switch to local stub when SANDBOX_MODE=true and no network? (useful for offline demos)

Notes to self / scribbles:
- Keep the first-run footprint under 20 files in repo - single HTML demo + server shim + concierge-lite package
- Provide two starter templates: chat-assistant and doc-embed-retriever
- Consider a very small Go example for infra teams that prefer typed clients

References and links:
- Confluence quick spec: CONFLUENCE-RED-2345 (proto: concierge brief)
- Internal GH template repo: git@github.com:redwood/concierge-quickstarts.git (branch: node-first)
- Related RFC: GH-PR-4821 (concierge-lite api sketch)
- Jira epic: JIRA-DE-987

Next steps (this week):
- [Maya] Draft the single-page quickstart with inlined curl examples (due Wed)
- [Diego] Ship concierge-lite alpha to npm internal registry and link in README (due Fri)
- [Priya] Wire Console temp telemetry toggle and confirm events flow (due next Tue)

If you're reading this as a champion: ping in #devex-concierge and I'll give you a pre-provisioned sandbox key and a tiny checklist to run through with your team.

-- end of notebook (working draft)
